newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New members would have to accept EMU - Parliament.
newsitem.headline: New members would have to accept EMU - Parliament.

text.p: The European Parliament said on Wednesday new members of the European Union would have to accept the plans for Economic and Monetary Union.
The Parliament, accepting a report by Greek European People's Party deputy Efthymios Christodoulou, said the Union should think and act carefully on the financial implications before enlargement.

"Enlargement should not be isolated as a separate issue from EMU," said the report, adding, "The new member states will have to accept it as an objective and commit themselves to pursuing an economic policy consistent with that objective."
The report said that the applicants should be obliged to go further in creating market economies, including pushing privatisation further and restructuring their public sectors.
They should also help generate the costs incurred by making conditions for private investment better.
The EU should increase its own resources before the end of the current financial perspectives expire in 1999, to help finance the enlargement, the Parliament said.
Also the Common Agricultural Policy should be revamped to bring prices more into line with world prices and structural policies should be improved.
The European Commission has said that the cost of extending the CAP to the applicants would be nine billion Ecus.

The Parliament report said that the applicant countries currently have lower farm prices, and that by raising them to EU levels families could be prevented from making savings, which could lead to social unrest.
At the same time the support levels were lower, it warned. By extending the EU system to the applicants the Union risked creating an upwards spiral in production.
The Parliament said that after the enlargement structual policies to help existing members should be continued and that this was an essential condition of the enlargement.
